environment.architecture: Timber-and-coral-stone buildings climbing the harbor bluffs in uneven terraces; salvaged old-kingdom masonry reused as foundation stone throughout the older quarters.
environment.activity: Dive crews hauling gear to the docks at dawn, guild criers reading the day's licensed sites, a constant traffic of handcarts moving salvage from harbor to market.
environment.sensory: Salt, tar, and drying kelp; the clatter of winches; gulls and the distant clang of the Drowned Bell marking the tide.
environment.lighting: Bright and glaring at midday off the water; oil-lamp lit and rowdy after dark, especially near the harbor.

curiosities.detail: Old-kingdom stonework is visible in half the building foundations, if you know to look for the archaic lettering.
Everyone in Port Calder has a story about someone who dove too deep and came back wrong, or didn't come back at all.

environment.architecture: A natural deepwater cove walled in by old breakwaters, half of them salvaged old-kingdom seawall stone.
environment.activity: Dive boats, salvage barges, and Concordat inspection skiffs crowd the water; crews load and unload from dawn to dusk.
environment.sensory: Rope and tar, brine, the groan of hulls against pilings.
environment.lighting: Open sky; lantern-strung at night along the seawall.

curiosities.detail: A section of old breakwater stone bears worn old-kingdom carvings, half-submerged at low tide.

environment.architecture: A blocky, well-kept stone hall facing the harbor, Concordat blue-and-gold banners over the door.
environment.activity: Queues of divers waiting on permits; clerks stamping manifests; a guard or two watching the line.
environment.sensory: Ink, wax seals, the murmur of paperwork disputes.

curiosities.detail: The public manifest board is missing several recent dive-site postings — quietly pulled, not officially cancelled.

environment.architecture: A sprawl of wooden piers, some newer construction, some visibly built on older stone pilings.
environment.activity: Dive crews prepping gear, dockhands haggling over cargo, licensed and unlicensed boats jockeying for berths.
environment.sensory: Wet rope, fish, low tide mud at the pier bases.

curiosities.detail: One unmarked pier at the far end sees regular traffic at odd hours — no Concordat flag, no manifest posted.

environment.architecture: A weathered two-story shack on stilts at the harbor mouth, signal flags and a tide-bell strung from the roof.
environment.activity: Tide and weather postings, berth assignments, incident reports.
environment.sensory: Damp wood, lamp oil, chalk dust from the tide-board.

curiosities.detail: The harbormaster logs every unusual find and current shift with more care than her pay grade requires — she's tracking something.

environment.architecture: A massive green-black bronze bell, old-kingdom make, raised from the reef decades ago and hung in a timber frame at the harbor mouth.
environment.activity: Rung on the hour by a rotating duty-watch; a minor local landmark and meeting point.
environment.sensory: A low, resonant tone that carries over the whole harbor; faint verdigris smell of old bronze.

curiosities.detail: The bell's old-kingdom inscription isn't a maker's mark — it's a warning, in a dialect none of Port Calder's scholars fully recognize.
The bell was cast as part of the original containment working. Ringing it in a specific pattern (unknown to the surface) can be felt below.

environment.architecture: Covered stalls and permanent shopfronts climbing the bluff terraces above the harbor, in uneven tiers.
environment.activity: Salvage appraisers weighing hauls in the open, food carts, guild criers reading the day's dive postings.
environment.sensory: Fry-oil and brine, competing vendor calls, coin counted loudly to discourage shortchanging.
environment.lighting: Awning-shaded by day; lantern-strung food stalls after dark.

curiosities.detail: An appraiser openly low-balls anything the Concordat hasn't pre-approved — a quiet way of steering unlicensed finds out of the market.
A stall further back sells "curios" that look a lot more genuine than they should. See [[saltbone_curios]].

environment.architecture: A tight row of narrow shopfronts wedged between the market and the docks, every one crammed floor to ceiling with gear.
environment.activity: Crews outfitting before a dive, apprentices pressure-testing helm seals, haggling over warded gear.
environment.sensory: Oiled leather, brass polish, the hiss of bladders under pressure-test.
environment.lighting: Workshop lamps; occasional sparks from a smith's stall.

curiosities.detail: One outfitter's gear consistently outperforms what a Concordat license should allow to be sold — she has an unlicensed supplier.

environment.architecture: A broad, low timber tavern built from retired ship's timbers, with a second floor of let rooms.
environment.activity: Dive crews trading stories and contracts over ale; a corkboard of job postings by the door.
environment.sensory: Woodsmoke, spilled ale, brine off wet oilskins drying by the hearth.
environment.lighting: Hearth-fire and oil lamps; warm and smoky.

curiosities.detail: Part of the job-postings corkboard carries no Concordat seal at all — informal, word-of-mouth contracts.

Recommended default home base / rest location for the party. The innkeeper trades in quiet information as readily as ale — a strong candidate for a Freedivers-adjacent contact NPC once that faction is authored (t008).

environment.architecture: A cramped, cluttered shopfront wedged behind the Market Quarter's main stalls.
environment.activity: Quiet transactions; an owner who asks very few questions.
environment.sensory: Dust, old brine, a faint ozone-tang off half-charged relics.

curiosities.detail: Several shelf items are genuine, low-grade old-kingdom relics that were never registered with the Concordat.
A quiet fence for crews avoiding Concordat tax — the owner is a good seed for a Freedivers-aligned NPC once that faction is authored (t008).

environment.architecture: Cramped tenements built shoulder-to-shoulder along the tideline, patched with salvage timber and old-kingdom stone block.
environment.activity: Dockworker families, nets drying on lines, children working the tide pools at low water.
environment.sensory: Wet laundry, low-tide mud, cookfire smoke.
environment.lighting: Dim, close alleys; a handful of public lamps at corners.

curiosities.detail: Tidewrack gossip travels faster than the guild boards — a good place to hear what's really happening below before it's official.

environment.architecture: Taller, denser housing built up rather than out, mixing building styles from a dozen homelands.
environment.activity: A rotating string of street-shrines and festivals, communal courtyards shared across households.
environment.sensory: Layered cooking smells, overlapping languages, wind chimes and hung charms.
environment.lighting: Strings of colored lanterns between buildings after dark.

curiosities.detail: A small courtyard shrine doesn't match any faith known to the ward's residents — recently added, and quietly well-tended.

environment.architecture: A squat stone blockhouse retrofitted from an old-kingdom seawall tower — patched, but sturdy.
environment.activity: Recruit drills, incident-report processing, a duty board that's perpetually short-staffed.
environment.sensory: Oiled steel, chalk dust, the creak of the old tower stair.

curiosities.detail: The duty board lists three "unresolved" incidents out of the Shallows with no follow-up logged — understaffing, or something being quietly buried.

environment.architecture: A modest multi-faith chapel and healer's hall, built partly from a reclaimed old-kingdom shrine's stone.
environment.activity: Healers tending dive injuries, an open shrine room welcoming any faith, a small ossuary for the unclaimed drowned.
environment.sensory: Incense, clean linen, a faint salt-damp in the older stonework.
environment.lighting: Candlelight; a skylight over the shrine room.

curiosities.detail: The chapel keeps careful record of every diver who never surfaced — meant as remembrance, but it's also the closest thing Port Calder has to a casualty log.
The reused old-kingdom stone in the shrine room is subtly warm to the touch, always, regardless of weather.

environment.architecture: A shallow ridge of serrated coral just past the harbor mouth, growing over buried, unnaturally straight stonework.
environment.activity: Crowded with training dives and licensed contract crews by midmorning; a handful of solitary night-fishers and freedivers after dusk.
environment.sensory: Bright, close water; the click and rasp of coral against dive gear.

curiosities.detail: The coral grows in unnaturally straight rows along buried stonework beneath the reef.

environment.architecture: A wide, bowl-shaped reef depression with a slow, permanent current gyre at its center.
environment.activity: Heavily licensed and inspected salvage dives; every crew that works it files a report.
environment.sensory: A constant low churn of silt and current; colder water than the surrounding reef.

curiosities.detail: Debris at the bowl's center skews far older and stranger than the surrounding reef.

environment.architecture: A flat, sunlit reef terrace in exceptionally clear, shallow water.
environment.activity: Guild licensing exams, demonstrations, and apprentice training dives by day; nearly empty after dark.
environment.sensory: Bright glare off the water; unusually quiet compared to other dive sites.

curiosities.detail: A few longtime divers avoid the Shelf despite its safety, muttering that "picked clean" doesn't mean empty.

environment.architecture: A stand of tall, blade-thin coral spires that comb the current into unpredictable channels.
environment.activity: Rarely dived except as a deliberate rite of passage; the Concordat licenses it at a steep price.
environment.sensory: Sharp currents, the whistle of water forced between narrow spires.

curiosities.detail: No two charts of the Combs agree — the spires shift position slightly between dives.

environment.architecture: A low reef shoal scattered with old-kingdom debris — glass, chain, bell fragments.
environment.activity: Cheaply licensed, rarely worked for salvage; quiet Drowned Choir pilgrimages on certain tide-nights.
environment.sensory: A faint hum through the water and hull on the right tide.

curiosities.detail: Small offerings — coins, carved wood, returned relics — are left scattered across the shoal.

environment.architecture: Half a dozen wrecks fused into one tangled reef by decades of coral growth and shifting sand.
environment.activity: Loud and crowded by day with staggered licensed crews; unlicensed wreck-pickers work it unmarked after dark.
environment.sensory: Groaning timber, hissing shifted sand, the metallic tang of old iron fittings.

curiosities.detail: One wreck's hull timbers are centuries older than the rest and driven into the tangle rather than sunk alongside it.

environment.architecture: An intact merchant marriage-barge resting upright in a sand hollow, masts snapped but hull whole.
environment.activity: A perennial favorite for licensed crews; storm-shifted sand exposes new cargo each season.
environment.sensory: Hazy gold light through the broken upper deck by morning; arm's-length visibility by afternoon current.

curiosities.detail: A sealed dowry chest sits untouched in the lower hold despite decades of open salvage.

environment.architecture: A raider longship's broken ribs jutting from a sand shelf, hull split nearly in two.
environment.activity: Rarely worked; crews that still take contracts here dive in daylight, in pairs, and don't linger.
environment.sensory: Unexplained cold pockets in the water; the creak of shifting wreckage.

curiosities.detail: Fresh scrape marks scar the ribs' inner hull, too large and too recent to be old salvage damage.

environment.architecture: A modest Concordat records-cutter, hull deliberately scored open along one seam.
environment.activity: Officially 'lost with all documents' two years back; never licensed for salvage, no exceptions.
environment.sensory: A sealed strongbox visible through a breached cabin window.

curiosities.detail: The hull's scoring is even and deliberate, clearly tool-made — not storm damage.

environment.architecture: A trade galley whose cargo hold burst open on impact, scattering old-kingdom glass cargo across the sand.
environment.activity: A frequent source for illicit curio stock; Drowned Choir pilgrims comb it clean on certain low tides.
environment.sensory: Scattered glints of light through murky water even at midday; sharp shards underfoot.

curiosities.detail: Several glass fragments are etched with old-kingdom script, intact enough to translate.

environment.architecture: A broad, largely intact paved road sloping down from the reef flats into deeper dark.
environment.activity: Concordat survey crews plant a numbered marker along it each season; no formal chart of its end exists.
environment.sensory: A faint, steady downward current pull that strengthens with depth.

curiosities.detail: The paving stones carry formal, titled old-kingdom script, distinct from any reused surface salvage stone.

environment.architecture: Two broken gate-towers flanking a collapsed formal archway, lintel stone still legibly inscribed.
environment.activity: A common turnaround point for licensed crews; a handful of 'beyond the gate' rumors trade like currency.
environment.sensory: A noticeable cold pressure change past the arch, like a doorway that isn't there anymore.

curiosities.detail: Two distinct sets of tool-marks scar the archway, one old-kingdom, one recent and not Concordat work.

environment.architecture: A wide formal stairway in even, deliberate steps, empty statuary alcoves lining the walls.
environment.activity: Technically off-limits without a Concordat writ; a rule enforced about as often as depth discourages visitors anyway.
environment.sensory: A faint, regular pulse of cold current from the alcoves, like slow breathing.

curiosities.detail: Every alcove carries a worn, carved name beneath it, none matching any figure known to Port Calder's history.

environment.architecture: Rows of modest, formally-built rowhouses in orderly ranks along a straight street grid.
environment.activity: Popular low-risk independent salvage; Freedivers use it to train new divers on room-to-room search.
environment.sensory: Deep-drifted sand in every lower room; kelp curtains in doorless frames.

curiosities.detail: Every house still bears its formal door-name plaque, oddly undamaged for otherwise fully collapsed structures.

environment.architecture: Dozens of fluted pillars standing in formal ranks around a roofless processional plaza.
environment.activity: Licensed only for supervised survey work as a 'heritage site' — not worth the guild's trouble to loot.
environment.sensory: Unusually good visibility for the depth; a faint tonal hum between pillars on certain tides.

curiosities.detail: Faint remnant wards cling to several pillars — old-kingdom protective work, long depleted but not fully dead.

environment.architecture: A sheltered reef cave mouth opening into a chain of air-pocketed grottoes, low ceilings hung with soft coral.
environment.activity: Freedivers use the outer chamber to train newcomers on breath control and confined-space work; the inner chambers are informally off-limits.
environment.sensory: Trapped air pockets that smell faintly of sulfur; the cave amplifies every sound, including things that aren't quite an echo.
environment.lighting: Dark past the outer chamber — most crews work it by lamp only at slack tide, when the current stops fighting the entrance.

curiosities.detail: Something has been dragging prey remains into the third chamber and stacking the bones with unsettling neatness.

environment.architecture: A dense, rootless kelp forest rooted in buried old-kingdom rubble, fronds tall enough to blot out the surface glow.
environment.activity: Licensed crews string guide-lines between numbered marker buoys before entering; solo divers who skip the lines have a bad habit of not resurfacing on schedule.
environment.sensory: Cold pockets between kelp stands; a rhythmic clacking of buoy-bells overhead that gets harder to place the deeper you go.
environment.lighting: Green-gold and dappled by day; the marker buoys carry small lanterns that Concordat crews light before dusk dives.

curiosities.detail: The kelp stands are subtly denser in a spiral pattern radiating from the forest's center — not natural growth.

environment.architecture: A mid-sized fishing trawler resting level on a sand shelf, sails long rotted but hull and rigging otherwise intact.
environment.activity: Harbor Watch keeps it nominally closed pending an incident review that's gone nowhere in three years; nothing stops unlicensed crews from working it anyway.
environment.sensory: Nets still coiled on deck, heavy with a catch that never got hauled in; unnervingly little marine growth on the hull for its age.
environment.lighting: Sits in open sand with good ambient light — the wreck is easy to see coming, which somehow makes it worse.

curiosities.detail: The ship's log, still legible in the waterlogged cabin, ends mid-sentence — no storm noted, no distress called, just silence.

The Marrow's full crew of nine were never found, alive or dead. This is the third of harbor_watch_garrison's three unresolved duty-board incidents (see harbor_watch_garrison.html) — the only one with no bodies and no obvious cause, which is precisely why Harbor Watch keeps burying the file instead of closing it.

environment.architecture: A slim, fast ketch scuttled deliberately in a shallow sand cut, hull scored open along the keel rather than broken by wreck.
environment.activity: No Concordat record of the ship ever existing under this name; local rumor calls it a smuggler's boat, and local rumor is right.
environment.sensory: A false-bottomed hold, empty now but for packing straw and a lingering incense smell out of place on a fishing coast.
environment.lighting: Shallow enough to work by daylight, though the Choir prefers it moonless.

curiosities.detail: Fresh straw and rope-burn marks in the false-bottomed hold — it was used within the last season, not decades ago.

The Nightweigh is a Drowned Choir supply run, run by deacon_rill, ferrying relics out of saltbone_curios' unregistered stock and new converts in, under a name that dies as fast as the Concordat can flag it. A good later hook: the party stakes it out on a Choir run night.

environment.architecture: A long stretch of collapsed formal wall, old-kingdom boundary stones still standing at regular intervals along its length.
environment.activity: A second, lesser-known checkpoint to Aldergate Shoal's — Concordat surveyors mark it on charts as the outer edge of the 'licensed zone' proper.
environment.sensory: The boundary stones hum faintly underhand, each at a slightly different pitch from its neighbors.
environment.lighting: Open, sunlit water by day; the boundary stones catch and hold a little residual glow well after dusk, which no one has satisfactorily explained.

curiosities.detail: Each boundary stone bears a different formal old-kingdom title, as though marking the edge of nine separate estates rather than one wall.

environment.architecture: A broad formal landing at the base of the Warders' Stair, where dressed paving gives way to open dark — the last built surface before the reef floor simply falls away.
environment.activity: The furthest point most licensed Shallows crews will chart; a few worn mooring rings suggest someone once meant to keep coming back to this exact spot.
environment.sensory: Noticeably colder past the landing's edge; sound travels strangely, swallowed rather than echoed.
environment.lighting: The last reliable ambient light in the Shallows — lamps carried past this point are, by long habit, kept lit no matter the cost in oil.

curiosities.detail: The paving stones at the landing's very edge are worn smooth in a path leading down and out — not from salvage traffic, which stops here, but from something that used to.

Mark this as the literal transition point into the Drowned Districts once that region is authored (t016) — the Warders' Stair leads here, and the Last Landing is where a party first commits to going past the Shallows for good.

environment.architecture: A formal civic assembly hall, tiered stone benches in a collapsed half-dome, the old kingdom's seal still unbroken on the dais.
environment.activity: The first real Choir presence a party meets past the Shallows — converts hold small vigils here and won't fight to keep outsiders out, just watch closely.
environment.sensory: A cold draft through the broken vault carries chant-echo from somewhere deeper in the district.
environment.lighting: A handful of Choir lanterns strung along old rafter-lines; everything past their reach is true dark.

curiosities.detail: The benches are worn in patterns that suggest regular recent use, not decades of neglect.
The assembly dais still bears the old kingdom's formal seal, deliberately left unbroken by whoever gathers here now.

environment.architecture: A formal processional street of narrow townhouses, each still bearing a petitioner's plaque above its door.
environment.activity: A few Choir converts squat in the empty townhouses; otherwise quiet, the kind of quiet that makes salvage crews walk fast.
environment.sensory: Door-plaques are still legible under a film of silt if wiped clean.

curiosities.detail: The plaques list unresolved petitions — some naming plaintiffs against the crown itself.
One plaque bears a surname matching a known Port Calder founding family — a usable hook if the DM wants to tie a PC or NPC's lineage to the old kingdom.

environment.architecture: A soaring former high chapel, roof long gone, open straight up into black water — the Choir's true seat, of which the_drowned_bell above is only an echo.
environment.activity: Choir vigil-boats moor at the altar-rail around the clock; this is where Isolt Vane herself is most often found.
environment.sensory: Chant carries strangely through open water here, felt in the chest more than heard.

curiosities.detail: The altar mosaic depicts the kingdom either embraced or swallowed by something vast — worn just enough that which one is deliberately unclear.

This is where Isolt performs the Choir's binding-adjacent rites, unknowingly reinforcing rather than loosening the deal described in why_the_kingdom_drowned_mystery — a strong scene if the party ever needs to see her sincerity up close.

environment.architecture: The gutted undercroft of the district's old grain-mill — stalled wheels locked in silt, machinery frozen mid-turn.
environment.activity: Mostly abandoned; the Choir uses the tunnels beneath it as a discreet route between sites.
environment.sensory: Settling machinery groans occasionally, audible even through water.

curiosities.detail: One mill-wheel can still be forced to turn, opening a sealed passage beneath it.
That passage connects toward the_weeping_stair — a shortcut for a party that finds it early, worth rewarding rather than gating.

environment.architecture: A tight switchback stairway descending in stepped terraces, water sheeting visibly down every riser.
environment.activity: Little traffic — colder and darker than the rest of the district discourages casual passage.
environment.sensory: Noticeably colder with every landing; the water itself seems to thicken.

curiosities.detail: Mark this as the eventual continuation point deeper into the Drowned Districts and, later, toward the Deep Kingdom — the same threshold role the_last_landing played for the Shallows.

environment.architecture: A small formal courtyard dominated by a bronze statue gone entirely green, its face smoothed to near-blankness.
environment.activity: A quiet shrine annex; Sister Meck comes here alone more often than official Choir business explains.
environment.sensory: A faint metallic taste in the water near the statue's base.

curiosities.detail: The statue's face was deliberately defaced at some point in the kingdom's own history, not worn away by time.
A good spot for a private party–Meck scene — she prays here without an audience, which is unusual for the Choir.

environment.architecture: A fortified mausoleum-house, still sealed under old-kingdom state wardwork rather than religious protection.
environment.activity: Undisturbed — heavier silt than anywhere else in the district, no current, no Choir presence.
environment.sensory: An unnatural stillness; nothing here drifts the way it should.

curiosities.detail: The seal wards are state magic, not religious — whoever built this expected someone to come looking, eventually.
The chancellor's private papers inside can seed a real fragment of why_the_kingdom_drowned_mystery — a strong player-found-lore location.

environment.architecture: A barracks-like guardhouse, weapon racks rotted to iron ghosts of their shapes in the silt.
environment.activity: The old kingdom's equivalent of the Harbor Watch garrison; modern Harbor Watch has an unofficial, low-key interest in it.
environment.sensory: An old alarm-bell mechanism still hangs intact near the entrance.

curiosities.detail: The alarm mechanism, if triggered, still partially works — a clang carries a surprising distance underwater.
Usable hook for fenn_hurley or tam_ostler to quietly commission the party — Harbor Watch would rather know what's in here before the Concordat does.

environment.architecture: Rows of loom-houses, threads long rotted, loom-frames still standing in eerie orderly ranks.
environment.activity: A handful of independent squatters and Choir converts live here — one of the district's few genuinely mundane, low-dread spots.
environment.sensory: Quieter than most of the district; almost domestic.

curiosities.detail: A few looms have been recently restrung with scavenged wire and kelp-fiber — someone here is actually trying to weave again.
A good breather location between dread beats — low-stakes social encounters, minor salvage, no real danger.

environment.architecture: A claustrophobic network of vaulted cisterns and narrow flooded tunnels beneath the district.
environment.activity: The Choir's discreet passage between several sites; strong tidal currents make parts of it genuinely hazardous.
environment.sensory: Current strong enough in places to sweep an unbraced diver off course.

curiosities.detail: Functions as a shortcut network connecting several Drowned Districts sites once discovered — useful for pacing a return trip, not required for the main path.

environment.architecture: A long colonnade lined with hundreds of formal memorial markers, organized by old-kingdom district of origin rather than family.
environment.activity: The Choir tends the markers constantly, keeping the names legible against the silt.
environment.sensory: Solemn and undisturbed; even Choir converts lower their voices here.

curiosities.detail: Markers grouped by district rather than family suggest whole neighborhoods went down together, fast.
A strong site for Deacon Rill's most sincere, least cult-like scene — grief rather than dogma.

environment.architecture: A long flooded avenue of collapsed row-houses, oddly free of silt drift compared to neighboring streets.
environment.activity: Almost none — divers who work the district avoid lingering here without saying exactly why.
environment.sensory: A constant susurrus of whispering, never louder, never quite resolving into words, with no visible source.

curiosities.detail: The whispering seems to trail slightly behind wherever the party's light points, not ahead of it.
First deliberately 'clear' omen in the Drowned Districts — no longer as deniable as the Shallows' salt_warped_grouper, but still nothing a party can act against directly. Escalate sparingly.

environment.architecture: A fortified reliquary vault, old-kingdom masonry with the Concordat's newer pry-marks scarring the doors.
environment.activity: A standing Concordat salvage claim; Wick Tallow's licensing stamps are recent, meaning crews are still working it.
environment.sensory: Faint warmth off certain reliquary shelves, in water that should carry no warmth at all.

curiosities.detail: One emptied shelf's manifest tag has been quietly altered — someone logged a find as 'lost in transit' that clearly wasn't.

The site behind Coraline Bray's private incident ledger: a recent haul from here wasn't inert the way salvage should be. Feeds the faction's 'still-breathing salvage' hook — use as a rare, escalating incident, not a repeatable mechanic.

environment.architecture: A derelict set of canal locks and sluice gates, once used to manage the old kingdom's inner waterways.
environment.activity: The gates shift and groan on their own, slow and rhythmic, with no current strong enough to explain it.
environment.sensory: A low structural groan that divers who've heard [[the_drowned_bell]] rung topside swear keeps the same rhythm.

curiosities.detail: The groaning briefly synchronizes with the bell whenever it's rung above, then drifts back out of step over the following hour.
A physical, roughly-verifiable version of the omen tone — not proof of anything supernatural on its own, but a strong beat for a party starting to connect the bell to something deeper.

environment.architecture: A sunken garden-hollow behind a collapsed manor wall, once ornamental, now a dead zone of bare stone.
environment.activity: A Freedivers survey site; Ivo Marlstone has pushed twice to chart it further despite the crew's unease.
environment.sensory: Noticeably colder than the surrounding district; no fish, no growth, no scavengers — total, unnatural quiet.

curiosities.detail: Even scavenger fish that pick at every other wreck in the district give this hollow a wide, consistent berth.
Ivo's ambition (seeded in t008) versus Ruen/Sela's caution can come to a head here — a good site for that internal Freedivers tension to surface in play.

environment.architecture: A records hall tilted hard on a collapsed foundation, shelving racked at an unsettling angle but largely intact.
environment.activity: [[sister_meck]] has been quietly working this site alone, against Choir custom of never reading the old records unsupervised.
environment.sensory: Undisturbed dust-silt on most shelves except one cleared, well-lit-by-lantern reading nook.

curiosities.detail: A surviving civic decree references sealing 'the lower wards' on the sovereign's own order, days before the water came — not an accident, an evacuation.
The first non-Choir textual fragment supporting [[why_the_kingdom_drowned_mystery]]. Ties directly to Sister Meck's doubt arc (seeded t009) — this is where her private research happens.

environment.architecture: A processional bridge of formal old-kingdom stonework, spanning a wide flooded plaza beneath [[vantmoor_hall]].
environment.activity: Little foot traffic; the span is structurally sound but avoided out of habit rather than danger.
environment.sensory: When [[the_drowned_bell]] rings topside, it isn't heard here so much as felt — a pressure change underwater ears shouldn't register.

curiosities.detail: A clean, repeatable way to let the party physically feel the bell's reach without any direct confirmation of what it means — good for building dread before the Deep Kingdom chapters.

environment.architecture: An open courtyard ringed with worn devotional carvings, adjoining [[verdigris_court]].
environment.activity: The Choir gathers here for call-and-response chants at set hours; attendance has grown in recent months.
environment.sensory: On the last few gatherings, something has answered the chant's final response line back — faint, wrong, and not from any Choir throat.

curiosities.detail: [[deacon_rill]] treats the answering echo as proof of the Choir's faith; [[sister_meck]] treats it as the first real evidence something is badly wrong.
A strong wedge scene for Sister Meck's arc — she can pull a sympathetic party aside here without breaking from the Choir outright.

environment.architecture: A short close of modest old-kingdom townhouses, better preserved than most of the district.
environment.activity: Genuinely quiet — no Choir presence, no salvage claims, just settled silt and closed doors.
environment.sensory: The closest thing the Drowned Districts offer to peaceful; even the ambient dread eases here.

curiosities.detail: A few homes still have undisturbed personal effects — the kind of ordinary, human detail easy to miss between omens and salvage.
Deliberate low-dread breather site between heavier beats — use it to pace tension, not to hide anything major.

environment.architecture: A converted almshouse, old-kingdom bones with practical Choir repairs — nothing ornamental, all function.
environment.activity: [[deacon_rill]] runs supply and shelter here for stragglers, lapsed converts, and the occasional lost diver.
environment.sensory: Warm lantern-light and mended nets; the most welcoming space the Choir maintains anywhere in the district.

curiosities.detail: Deliberately humanizing site for the Choir — genuine charity, no hidden agenda here. Good place for a party to owe the Choir a real, uncomplicated debt before the campaign pushes toward opposition.

environment.architecture: A monumental formal gatehouse, once a toll checkpoint into the old kingdom's inner wards.
environment.activity: Disputed ground: [[harbor_watch]] patrols it as an extension of [[ashgate_wardhouse]]'s beat, while the Concordat claims salvage rights on the gatehouse vaults.
environment.sensory: Fresh rope and lantern-oil residue from both Watch patrols and Concordat crews, neither acknowledging the other's presence.

curiosities.detail: Neither faction has filed a formal complaint about the other — both would rather quietly coexist than draw attention to what's really behind the gate.
A low-stakes jurisdiction friction site — useful if the party ever needs a faction favor and has to pick a side, however small.

environment.architecture: A raised formal speaking platform facing a collapsed public square, near [[the_chancellors_rest]].
environment.activity: Silent and empty — the old kingdom's court of public appeals, long since adjourned.
environment.sensory: The platform is oddly undamaged compared to the ruined square facing it, as if the water rose around it rather than through it.

curiosities.detail: A weathered but legible inscription references a final address given from this rostrum — a sovereign's decree, not a plea for rescue.
Pairs with [[the_leaning_archive]]'s sealed-wards decree — together they build the picture that the drowning was ordered, not suffered, feeding [[why_the_kingdom_drowned_mystery]].

environment.architecture: The flooded machinery pit of an old kingdom watermill, wheel and gearing still largely intact.
environment.activity: Both [[freedivers]] and [[salvage_concordat]] crews work it in rotation for scrap-metal contracts.
environment.sensory: Rusted gearing groans and shifts under current, snagging unwary divers on jagged, half-turning teeth.

curiosities.detail: Straightforward hazard/salvage site — jammed machinery as an environmental obstacle, no supernatural weight needed here. Useful as a mechanical breather between omen-heavy sites.

environment.architecture: A private aristocratic vault-chamber, built into a collapsed manor cellar, still sealed by a corroded formal lock.
environment.activity: Unclaimed by the Concordat's official manifests — [[coraline_bray]] knows it exists and hasn't logged it.
environment.sensory: Fine ash-grey silt coats everything inside, undisturbed for centuries, faintly luminous under lantern-light.

curiosities.detail: A single item among the ash has clearly been handled recently, then carefully replaced exactly where it was.
Seed site for a future mid-game item entity (t026) — hold the specific relic open until that task, but the hook (Coraline's undisclosed interest) is live now.

environment.architecture: A final formal stairwell, wider and colder than [[the_weeping_stair]] above it, descending past the last intact district wall.
environment.activity: Nothing lives at this depth; even the Choir does not linger past this point.
environment.sensory: Absolute cold and absolute dark beyond lantern range — pressure a diver feels in their teeth, not just their ears.

curiosities.detail: Marks the transition threshold out of the Drowned Districts and into the Deep Kingdom (t021+), the same structural role [[the_last_landing]] played between the Shallows and here. Hold any Deep Kingdom content until those tasks.

environment.architecture: A monumental twin-towered gatehouse at full original height, doors long rotted from intact titanic hinges.
environment.activity: Nothing moves here voluntarily; this is the first Deep Kingdom site most parties reach.
environment.sensory: Unnerving stillness — no current, no drift, water that barely seems to move at all past the threshold.

curiosities.detail: The lintel inscription is a formal title addressed to whoever approaches, in a register no living Port Calder scholar fully reads.

environment.architecture: A grand processional avenue wide enough for a twenty-abreast procession, flanked by empty statuary plinths.
environment.activity: The capital's hub — side avenues branch toward the Hold, the Terrace, and the Chancellery.
environment.sensory: Lantern light feels smaller here than anywhere above; the scale was built for a light source no diver carries.

curiosities.detail: Every plinth plaque names a title and a date, never a person — a formal honor roll, not a memorial.

environment.architecture: A fortified barracks-monument, entry hall lined with intact carved-name alcoves, each now paired with a worn statuary bust.
environment.activity: A possible warden_husk patrol still walks a fixed route through the hall.
environment.sensory: Cold, formal, and very quiet — the hush of a garrison that stood its last post and was never relieved.

curiosities.detail: Several busts are deliberately defaced, not by time; the roll's gaps cluster together rather than scattering at random.

environment.architecture: A tiered aristocratic residential quarter, town-houses stacked up a gentle rise in diminishing grandeur.
environment.activity: Untouched since the drowning — doors open or missing, nothing looted, nothing disturbed.
environment.sensory: Melancholy rather than horror — a life mid-sentence, interrupted and never resumed.

curiosities.detail: Personal effects remain in nearly every house — a set table, a child's toy on a stair, a wardrobe never emptied.

environment.architecture: A fortress-palace complex housing the old kingdom's seat of governance, its state archive hall largely intact.
environment.activity: Nothing moves; the archive seals remain unbroken, waiting the way an unfinished meeting waits.
environment.sensory: One chamber's furniture is still arranged for a session that was never adjourned.

curiosities.detail: The archive seals bear a chancellor's formal seal-mark, matching the one on the_chancellors_rest's door exactly.

environment.architecture: The old capital's central marketplace, stalls standing in orderly rows.
environment.activity: Frozen mid-transaction — shutters drawn, stalls tidied, coin still sitting in more than one abandoned till.
environment.sensory: Human-scale and quiet, a normal night that was never resumed rather than a disaster scene.

curiosities.detail: Coin remains untouched in stall-tills throughout the market — a fortune in old-kingdom currency, worthless to modern buyers but a curiosity to collectors.

environment.architecture: The processional terminus of [[aurewake_concourse]] — a domed audience hall raised on a stepped dais, built to be seen from the avenue's full length.
environment.activity: Utterly still; the hall's acoustics amplify even a diver's own bubbles into something like a held breath.
environment.sensory: A cold, clean draft that shouldn't exist this deep moves through the dome — the first sign in the Deep Kingdom that something down here still circulates on its own terms.

curiosities.detail: The dais holds no throne — an empty plinth, the seat itself removed as deliberately as the statues on [[aurewake_concourse]].
Wall reliefs depict a coronation rite that matches no ritual practiced anywhere in modern Port Calder, old-kingdom or Choir.
The unexplained draft is the campaign's first non-symbolic hint that [[it_that_kept_the_kingdom]] is close and active, not merely a story — keep it as atmosphere, never a direct manifestation here.

environment.architecture: A sealed strongroom beneath [[warders_hold]], reached by a stair the Wardens' roll marks as restricted, guarded rather than merely locked.
environment.activity: Sealed since the drowning — the vault door shows tool-marks from a deliberate, orderly locking, not a hasty one.
environment.sensory: Absolute silence inside the seal; even current and drift stop dead at the threshold, as though the room itself is holding still.

curiosities.detail: Shelving racks are three-quarters empty and neatly so — most of the treasury was deliberately removed, not looted, before the seal went up.
What remains is modest by treasury standards: coin, minor regalia, and a handful of sealed document tubes — the valuable things clearly went somewhere else on purpose.
Good seed location for a future item entity (t026) — a minor regalia piece or a sealed document tube makes a natural, low-stakes find here. A [[warden_husk]] may still be posted at the inner seal.

environment.architecture: A circular sanctum off [[the_regnants_seat]], its walls carved floor-to-ceiling with a binding-rite in relief — the same iconography [[the_hollow_choir_yard]] echoes above, but whole here, and clearly the original rather than a copy.
environment.activity: Undisturbed by the Choir, who venerate this rite without having ever actually reached this room.
environment.sensory: The carvings seem to draw what little light a lantern casts, leaving the rest of the sanctum darker than the water outside should allow.

curiosities.detail: The relief depicts the binding as a covenant struck willingly, not a spell cast in desperation — a nuance the modern Choir's teachings have lost entirely.
A working still faintly active in the stone confirms the binding is a covenant, not a one-time casting — it requires something ongoing to hold, which lines up with [[the_breaking_deal_mystery]].

The strongest single location for a player who wants to understand the Choir sympathetically — they're not wrong that something was sacred here, only wrong about what freeing it would mean. Do not let this room resolve [[the_breaking_deal_mystery]] outright; it clarifies the nature of the deal, not its remaining lifespan.

environment.architecture: A tall, narrow scholars' tower off [[drowned_chancellery]], its upper chamber ringed with brass instrument-mounts whose actual instruments are long gone.
environment.activity: Abandoned mid-use — star-charts and tide-tables left pinned open rather than shelved.
environment.sensory: The tower's height puts a diver above the worst of the ambient silt; visibility here is the best anywhere in the Deep Kingdom, which only makes the empty instrument-mounts more conspicuous.

curiosities.detail: The pinned-open charts track tidal and astronomical cycles obsessively in the final months' entries — someone here was trying to time something.
Annotations cross-reference the charts against a ritual calendar, not a navigational one — this was a working being scheduled, not weather being predicted.

Pairs directly with [[the_leaning_archive]]'s sealed decree — the scholars here were calculating the correct timing for the binding-working itself, another concrete plank in the 'evacuation, not disaster' case for [[why_the_kingdom_drowned_mystery]].

environment.architecture: A long memorial hall off [[the_regnants_seat]], lined with portrait-reliefs of the old royal line in unbroken succession, down to a final frame.
environment.activity: Quiet and orderly — a place kept, not abandoned in haste, in the same register as [[vaelgard_terrace]].
environment.sensory: Cold stone made colder by scale; the final portrait-frame is noticeably larger than the rest, as if built for a likeness that was never finished.

curiosities.detail: The succession is unbroken and complete — every ruler accounted for, right up to the last, unfinished frame.
The final frame's relief is roughed in but not carved to completion, tools left neatly beside it rather than dropped mid-work.

The unfinished final portrait is a quiet, human-scale echo of [[drowned_chancellery]]'s unfinished draft document — the same last ruler, caught mid-decision in two different rooms. Keep both discoveries available independently; a party that finds this before the Chancellery should still feel the weight without needing the other to explain it.

environment.architecture: A final descending stair behind [[ilyndras_sanctum]], narrower and less formal than anything else in the capital core, as if it were never meant to be a public way.
environment.activity: The last stretch of the old kingdom built for people; past its bottom step, nothing here was built for anyone.
environment.sensory: Pressure and cold deepen sharply past the first few steps, and the earlier draft from [[the_regnants_seat]] resolves here into a slow, directional pull — something down there is drawing water toward itself.

curiosities.detail: The pull is faint but constant, strongest at the stair's lowest visible landing — current with a clear source, in water that shouldn't have current at all.

Marks the threshold out of the capital core and toward the containment site of [[it_that_kept_the_kingdom]] (t023/t024) — the same structural role [[the_last_descent]] played entering the Deep Kingdom. Hold any direct containment-site content until those tasks; this location is dread and anticipation only.

environment.architecture: A long colonnade at the base of [[threshwater_stair]], pillars in even ranks, hundreds of kneeling statues facing a single direction in unhurried genuflection.
environment.activity: The old kingdom's pilgrimage route, walked on a fixed calendar toward whatever waits at its far end — reverence, not terror, carved into every figure.
environment.sensory: The directional pull from the stair sharpens here, strongest exactly where the statues face; faded old-tongue script runs along the lower pillar band.

curiosities.detail: Every statue's base holds a shallow, long-emptied offering-niche.
Five statues near the midpoint have been deliberately turned to face back the way the party came.
The repeated inscription is a plea for continuation, not release — that the debt keep being paid, not that the arrangement end.

environment.architecture: A private side-chamber off [[suppliants_colonnade]], unceremonial, holding a stone seat, a bronze writing table, and walls of tightly-carved personal text.
environment.activity: The private record of Mireth, a Warden who oversaw the binding's containment work in its final years — dutiful reports giving way to something closer to confession.
environment.sensory: The carving hand shifts noticeably partway through the far wall; the room feels different by the time the text breaks off mid-sentence.

curiosities.detail: The tone shift from official report to private confession is precisely placeable partway along the far wall.
The five reversed statues at the colonnade's midpoint are named and explained here as Mireth's own act.
The final passage cuts off because Mireth stopped writing here and was never recorded again — see DM Notes.

environment.architecture: A low workshop-archive off [[suppliants_colonnade]], racks of fist-sized ward-stones connected by corroded bronze conduit deeper into the ruin.
environment.activity: The workshop of the old kingdom's Ward-Wrights, tools still racked in order as though they meant to return; roughly a third of the ward-stones have gone dark.
environment.sensory: The failed stones are scattered evenly through the racks rather than clustered — slow, uniform failure, not a single point of damage.

curiosities.detail: Schematic tablets trace the ward-stone network toward [[cindrel_vault]] and toward [[velmarch_spire]]'s original working-schedule.
A half-finished replacement ward-stone sits on a workbench, tools laid down mid-work.
A single larger, more heavily worked master ward-stone sits apart from the standard stock — see [[the_wardwrights_binding_seal]].

environment.architecture: A long open stretch between two rock faces past the undercroft — clearly widened, never built, with no old-kingdom architecture at all.
environment.activity: The last stretch before whatever is being contained; nothing here attacks, because nothing here needs to.
environment.sensory: Sound flattens and swallows itself unnaturally; bioluminescent growth present everywhere else simply stops at an unmarked line.

curiosities.detail: Bioluminescence stops abruptly a short distance in, as if it never took root beyond that point.
Every sound — breath, whisper, dropped tool — rings wrong-close, swallowed almost before it starts.
Old lantern-anchors at regular intervals stopped being maintained well before the kingdom drowned, not after.

environment.architecture: A pair of thirty-foot ward-carved stone gate-leaves set into deliberately cut rock at the end of [[the_long_hush]] — built to close, not to welcome.
environment.activity: The literal threshold into the containment site, marked by a full-height crack and old repair scarring cracked open again.
environment.sensory: Current runs steadily through the crack, one direction, into the dark beyond — the source of the pull felt as far back as [[threshwater_stair]].

curiosities.detail: The crack is the source of the directional current felt throughout the region.
Old repair scarring around the crack is decades old at least; the crack itself is recent enough its edges haven't weathered smooth.
A single large ward-stone at the gate's center is visibly failing in real time — the clearest physical sign yet that the deal is breaking.

environment.architecture: Raw, unworked rock beyond the gate; ward-conduits from the network above dive straight into bare stone rather than kingdom masonry.
environment.activity: Three glyph-marked passages branch off a central shaft where the gate's current drops away and out of sight.
environment.sensory: The pull toward the shaft is the strongest felt anywhere in the region; loose gear drifts steadily toward it.

curiosities.detail: The three onward passages are individually marked with distinct glyph-sets, clearly meant to be chosen between.
Every surface here is bare rock or ward-conduit — nothing carved for habitation, worship, or record-keeping.
The shaft's pull is strongest here of anywhere in the Deep Kingdom.

environment.architecture: A cathedral-scale lattice of thousands of ward-stones covering every surface — the whole containment network's true heart.
environment.activity: Whole patches sit dark and failing, spreading outward from a scatter of identifiable failure-points.
environment.sensory: A low resonant hum from the working stones; the dark patches are silent by contrast.

curiosities.detail: A rough headcount puts the network at roughly two-thirds still functioning.
Failure-points cluster near specific stones whose loss would cascade fastest.
An unfinished alcove holds tools left mid-work, wired to nothing.

environment.architecture: A small side-chamber off the lattice's unfinished alcove, one wall carved wall-to-wall with a single unbroken legal text.
environment.activity: Undisturbed since it was carved.
environment.sensory: Formal old-tongue legal phrasing, clear enough to any reader who can parse the hand.

curiosities.detail: The text confirms the kingdom sank itself deliberately as the price of containment.
A witness-signatory listed at the text's foot matches Mireth's confession exactly.
A closing clause describes the deal as renewable "by hand and seal" — a pointer toward the renewal font.

environment.architecture: A sealed side-passage alcove holding an empty housing precisely shaped for a master ward-stone.
environment.activity: Unfinished rather than damaged — tool-scars sharp, conduit ends capped, dust settled evenly.
environment.sensory: The one part of the network showing no wear or decay at all.

curiosities.roll: No check needed (with item) / Investigation DC 14 (without)
curiosities.detail: The empty housing's shape matches the Ward-Wright's Binding Seal exactly.
The alcove shows no decay, unlike every other failure point in the region.
Conduit lines from the housing reach toward the deepest part of the lattice.

environment.architecture: A hastily-thrown-up barricade of collapsed stone and old war-material, statuary busts cracked or toppled.
environment.activity: A warden remnant still patrols the wreckage, sharper and more alert than the husks above.
environment.sensory: Real battle damage — scorch, breakage, gouges — unlike the untouched hush of Warders' Hold.

curiosities.detail: Damage reads as an assault from the inner side outward — the Wardens fought going the wrong direction.
A vigil-roster names match Warders' Hold's alcove busts, closing that thread.
The sentinel here challenges with more urgency and doesn't stand down as readily.

environment.architecture: A side-chamber camp left arranged and undisturbed, gear packed with care.
environment.activity: A Drowned Choir pilgrimage cell stopped here mid-purpose and never resumed.
environment.sensory: Hymnal pages scattered, marginalia growing more desperate, then more certain, then stopping.

curiosities.detail: Marginalia in the hymnal pages tracks the same hymns as the Drowned Hymnal, written by a hand growing more certain over time.
Nothing suggests panic or a fight — the camp was left in order, mid-purpose.
The final legible marginalia line reads like relief, not fear.

environment.architecture: An unshaped cave space; walls seem to lean inward a fraction more than measurement ever confirms.
environment.activity: The closest approach to It That Kept the Kingdom the site allows without full descent to the Undoing.
environment.sensory: Whispers in voices that resolve, briefly, into people the listener actually knows.

curiosities.detail: The whispers use recognizable voices drawn from people the listener has actually met.
A previous explorer's gear lies undisturbed near the entrance, set down and never picked back up.
The Unmade may be present, holding its shape longer and reacting faintly when spoken to.

environment.architecture: No walls in any conventional sense — the containment given physical shape, a hollow scooped out of the world.
environment.activity: Every passage from the site above rejoins here.
environment.sensory: The boundary between kingdom and what it kept holds thinnest anywhere in the region.

curiosities.detail: The three paths the site has offered are all physically enactable from this room, in whatever combination the party has prepared for.
It That Kept the Kingdom is present here in a way it has been nowhere else.
The chamber does not pressure a decision on a hard timer beyond whatever tension the table has built.
